questions.q: Why put TfidfVectorizer and LogisticRegression together in a single Pipeline?
options: Pipelines make logistic regression run faster
The vectorizer's vocabulary and IDF are then learned from training text only, and the same steps apply to new text
A classifier cannot accept a sparse matrix otherwise
Pipelines automatically remove stop words
questions.explain: The pipeline fits every step on training data only and reapplies the same transformations at prediction time, which prevents leakage and keeps the code tidy.

questions.q: Why did the lesson compare the 0.667 accuracy with a majority-class baseline of 0.333?
options: To show that the baseline is usually better
Because accuracy is only valid above 0.5
To show the model had learned something beyond guessing the most common class
To choose the regularization strength
questions.explain: An accuracy number means little without a reference. With three balanced classes, always guessing one class gets about 0.333.

questions.q: The single test split had 15 tickets and the five cross-validation folds scored from 0.67 to 0.83. What does that spread tell you?
options: The model is broken
Cross-validation always produces identical scores
The vectorizer was fit on the test set
With such a small dataset, any single score is noisy, so small differences between models are not trustworthy
questions.explain: With about 60 examples, each fold has only 12 tickets, so scores swing widely. Differences of a few points fall within that noise.

questions.q: In the coefficient plot, 'my' was the strongest word for the billing class. What is the best interpretation?
options: 'my' is the most important concept in billing
It is likely a quirk of this small sample: 15 of the 20 billing tickets happen to contain 'my'
The model must be using a bug in scikit-learn
Stop words can never carry any signal
questions.explain: The word appears in most billing tickets in this illustrative sample, so the model uses it. Inspecting coefficients helps you spot artifacts of the sample.

questions.q: What happened when stop_words="english" was added under the same 5-fold cross-validation?
options: The mean score fell from about 0.78 to 0.70, since words like 'how' and 'can' are signal for the how-to class
The mean score rose to 1.0
The pipeline raised an error
Nothing changed at all
questions.explain: Question words are informative for how-to tickets, so removing them hurt. Filtering words is not automatically an improvement; test it.
